request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows the signed-in user's crew total, and all 4 acceptance tests pass when run with `bin/e2e`.

**What it shows:** a new "My crew due total" figure (`data-testid="my-crew-due-total"`) next to the "My overdue total" figure. It finds the person whose name or alias matches the signed-in user (ignoring case), the same way "My due total" does. It then adds up the due-totals of every crew that person leads. It's blank if no person matches or that person leads no crew. Crews they're only a member of don't count.

**Where:**
- **New `features/crews/crewDue.ts`:** a small helper that works out a crew's due-total. I moved the existing logic out of `crews.slot.tsx` so the crew row and the header use the same rule.
- **`features/header/header.slot.tsx`:** loads the crews and shows the new figure.

It's a front-end-only change. Crews, their leads and due-totals were already available on the client, so the server and stored data didn't need to change, and no new audit records are written.
